theory.overview: Intermediate Representations (IR) bridge the gap between high-level source code and low-level machine code. IRs like SSA (Static Single Assignment), three-address code, and control flow graphs enable powerful optimizations. Understanding IR helps you grasp how compilers transform and optimize your code through multiple passes.

keyConcepts.title: Three-Address Code
keyConcepts.content: Each instruction has at most three operands: result = op1 operator op2. This simplifies analysis and transformation by breaking complex expressions into simple steps.

keyConcepts.title: SSA Form
keyConcepts.content: Static Single Assignment requires each variable to be assigned exactly once. This makes data flow explicit and enables powerful optimizations like constant propagation and dead code elimination.

keyConcepts.title: Basic Blocks & CFG
keyConcepts.content: A basic block is a sequence of instructions with no branches (except at end). The Control Flow Graph connects blocks showing possible execution paths, enabling global optimizations.

keyConcepts.title: Phi Functions
keyConcepts.content: In SSA, Phi (Φ) functions merge values from different predecessors. At a join point, Φ selects the appropriate value based on which path was taken.

steps.title: Converting to Three-Address Code
steps.content: Break complex expressions: 'a = b + c * d' becomes 't1 = c * d' then 'a = b + t1'. Each temp holds an intermediate result.

steps.title: SSA Construction
steps.content: Rename variables so each assignment is unique. Insert Phi functions at merge points where different values converge.

steps.title: Optimization Passes
steps.content: IR enables transformations: constant folding (compute at compile time), copy propagation (eliminate redundant copies), dead code elimination (remove unused computations).

practiceProblems.title: Convert to 3AC
practiceProblems.solution: t1 = a + b; t2 = c - d; x = t1 * t2

practiceProblems.title: SSA Form
practiceProblems.description: Convert: if (cond) x = 1 else x = 2; return x
practiceProblems.solution: if (cond) x1 = 1 else x2 = 2; x3 = Φ(x1, x2); return x3
